points.t: **Many naevi of varied size and colour** (often > 100), some atypical, ± a **family history of melanoma or pancreatic cancer**.
Inherited and UV risk (**CDKN2A**, CDK4, BAP1, MC1R) producing a high-naevus phenotype; most melanomas arise **de novo**.
Refer for **dermatology surveillance** (mole mapping + digital dermoscopy); **clinical genetics** if criteria met; sun protection; whole-skin self-checks.
Melanoma presenting as an ugly duckling; **pancreatic cancer** in CDKN2A families; BAP1 (uveal melanoma, mesothelioma).

cause.lead: A risk phenotype, sometimes a gene.
points: **FAMMM / CDKN2A** (p16): early, multiple melanomas; **pancreatic cancer** (~15–25% lifetime in some families).
**BAP1**: cutaneous and **uveal** melanoma, mesothelioma, renal cancer.
CDK4, telomere genes (POT1…); **MC1R** variants (red hair, freckles).
> 100 naevi ~7× risk; one first-degree relative ~2×; CDKN2A ~30–70% by 80.

visuals.caption: High-risk patients are followed with total-body photography and sequential digital dermoscopy so new or changing lesions stand out.
visuals.alt: Back with many moles beside a camera and dermatoscope

points: Many naevi on trunk and limbs, **varied sizes and colours**; atypical: > 5 mm, irregular, variegated.
Family pointers: onset < 40, multiple primaries, several relatives, pancreatic cancer.

visuals.caption: In a person with many moles, compare: the lesion that looks different is the one to worry about.

points: **Three-generation**: melanoma, pancreatic cancer, uveal melanoma, mesothelioma.
≥ 3 melanomas (individual / family), **melanoma + pancreatic cancer**, melanoma + mesothelioma / uveal (BAP1); counselling before testing.

cards.name: Sporadic multiple melanoma
cards.clue: High UV, fair skin, no family pattern.

points: **Dermatology** (routine): AMS phenotype, **≥ 2 first-degree relatives with melanoma**, or personal melanoma (NG14).
Total-body photography + **sequential digital dermoscopy every 3–12 months**; CDKN2A families: pancreatic surveillance programmes (e.g. EUROPAC).
Shade, UV clothing, hat, **SPF 30–50 reapplied every 2 h**; no sunbeds; no smoking.
Monthly **whole-skin** checks with partner / photos: most AMS melanomas arise de novo.

limits.t: UK Code: insurers can’t require predictive results (except very large policies / Huntington’s).

items.t: Multiple atypical naevi + family history of melanoma: **dermatology surveillance**.
Melanoma and pancreatic cancer in the same family: **clinical genetics** (CDKN2A).
Any changing outlier lesion: suspected cancer pathway.

pearls.t: **Most melanomas in AMS arise de novo**, so watch the whole skin, not one mole.
Ask about pancreatic cancer in the family.
